trust_decision.summary: Whether the session user may act on the given user's profile (profile image, pronunciation recording, profile fields) is decided by comparing the id of the current session user with the target user uuid, plus a superuser exemption; at the pinned commit only setProfileImage performs that comparison, and the other mutators trust the caller's uuid. The fix moves the comparison into ProfileServiceImpl.checkCanModifyProfile, exposes it as ProfileService.assertCanModifyProfile for the controller, and maps the thrown SecurityException to 403.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary is 'Profile Image Deletion has an IDOR', so the first place an engineer looks is the DELETE /api/users/{userId}/profile/image handler; it fetches the current user id, rejects only a null session, and then calls profileService.removeProfileImage(userId) with the path variable uncompared.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory names image deletion, so saveUserProfile and removePronunciationRecording can be argued to be a neighbouring feature (profile-field edit and pronunciation) behind different routes, already guarded by the canEdit/canUpdatePicture flags the service returns to the UI, leaving only DELETE /profile/image to fix.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Superusers must keep being able to modify and delete another user's image, recording and profile: the service advertises canEdit and canUpdatePicture as true for superusers and the picture/account UI relies on those flags, so an over-broad fix that only compares currentUserUuid.equals(targetUuid) with no isSuperUser exemption breaks admin support; the published fix keeps the exemption (its own test removeProfileImageAllowsSuperUser asserts it).

no authenticated session at all (null current user id vs missing Sakai session)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add an ownership comparison only in ProfileController.removeProfileImage (and removeNamePronunciation) against session.getUserId(), leaving ProfileService.removeProfileImage/saveUserProfile/removePronunciationRecording open to any direct caller and leaving the SecurityException-to-403 mapping absent.
